newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. unveils $68.2 bln revised budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. unveils $68.2 bln revised budget plan.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson unveiled a revised $68.2 billion budget plan on Wednesday that would aid cash-strapped local governments, and sharply increase state education and child care spending.

Reflecting California's strong economy, the Republican governor's new 1997-1998 budget spending plan was revised up from the $66.6 billion proposed in January. Wilson's revised budget calls for a reserve of $580 million for economic uncertainties, up from $553 million in January's budget plan.
Wilson's revised budget reflects the state's unexpected economic windfall, state officials said.

For the current year, general fund revenues are now forecast to come in $960 million more than anticipated by the Wilson administration in January, and $1.3 billion more than expected for the 1997-1998 budget year, for a combined increase of $2.26 billion, Wilson said.

"With a growing economy and more Californians working than ever before, this state finally has the revenues sufficient to make the kind of investments needed to address California's most urgent priorities," Wilson said in unveiling the plan.

Wilson's revised budget plan would boost education funding by $340 million, providing an additional $230 million to reduce class sizes, $60 million to fund standardized testing, and $50 million for classroom techology.
The revised budget includes a $440 million welfare-to-work plan that includes $50 million to capitalize the state infrastructure and economic development bank.

Wilson also proposed a $225 million package to aid the state's cash-strapped cities and counties. The package includes $100 million in property tax relief, $75 million in county hospital funding and $50 million for the state infrastructure bank to fund local projects.
